speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and was there any specific injury or event that preceded it?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail. Can you describe the mechanism of injury further—did the finger get pulled straight back (hyperextension) or was it bent to the side?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to flex the distal joint combined with the hyperextension mechanism strongly suggests a flexor tendon avulsion, often called a "Jersey finger." To confirm this, I need to see the anatomy of the tendon and any potential bone fragments. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mechanism of injury and your specific inability to flex the fingertip strongly point to an avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out a bony avulsion, I need to visualize the anatomy clearly. REQUEST TEST: MRI Right Hand

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying that there are no neurological symptoms like numbness, which helps rule out nerve involvement. Given the history of forced hyperextension, the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint, and the tenderness, the clinical picture is classic for a flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Avulsion)
